title: Direct Play — Vertical Passes to Break Lines
content: Direct vertical play prioritises forward passes that skip lines of the opponent's defensive structure rather than building patiently through horizontal possession. A line-breaking pass goes from behind one defensive line to a player between two defensive lines — from behind the midfield press directly to a player between the midfield and defensive lines, or from midfield directly over the defensive line. The key is identifying the pocket between defensive lines and having a player positioned there to receive. Direct play is most effective against high-pressing teams (who leave space behind), when the opposition is transitioning and not organised, or when the team needs to inject urgency (losing late in a game). Risk: technical demand is high, and lost balls often occur in dangerous central positions.
